## Scientific Status

This volume is a living technical manuscript for research and engineering workflows.
It is not presented as peer-reviewed consensus material. Mathematical statements require their stated hypotheses; conclusions about golfers additionally require independent measurements and model validation.

## Mathematical Reference Appendices

The notation reference and appendices distinguish coordinate geometry, the sensitivity of a specified motion, and the additional conditions needed for stability or optimization. Parallel transport compares vectors; a state-transition map propagates perturbations. A positive-definite metric, a matrix exponential, or a successful numerical solve does not by itself establish stable face delivery.

The revised reference supplies controlled Jacobians, branch-aware rotation maps, power-preserving twist/wrench transformations, metric-weighted sensitivities, and the hypotheses behind matrix and solver formulas. Both printed Python examples are executable manufactured checks. This reference review does not certify every chapter or establish an empirical golf result.

[Read the Reviewed Manuscript PDF](https://github.com/D-sorganization/AffineDrift/raw/fbee4da94fd699e9710f4c29b42a73a5113f08d4/articles/The_Geometry_of_Motion/Volume_I/main.pdf){.resource-link}

## Chapter 1: Foundations: Tangent Spaces and Exactness {#book1-ch1}

The core thesis: for a differentiable model, at fixed state, time, and mode, perturbations map linearly to the first variation of the state rate. If the model is also control-affine, $\dot x=f_0(x,t)+G(x,t)u$, then a finite input increment $v$ changes the state rate by exactly $G(x,t)v$ while state, time and mode stay fixed, and the instantaneous force-to-acceleration map is affine in the declared input. In words: at that instant, the change in state rate is the input map times the change in input, however large the input change is. A taxi fare is a useful picture, with limits. A fare is a flag-drop plus a rate times the miles. Here the flag-drop is the acceleration that gravity and velocity-dependent forces produce with no input, and the rate card is the map from input to added acceleration. Because of the flag-drop, doubling the input need not double the acceleration, but extra input adds exactly the rate card times the extra input. Unlike a fare, the rate card is a matrix, so a push at one joint can change acceleration at others. And the picture holds only at one frozen instant and state (posture and velocity): when the state changes, both the flag-drop and the rate card change, so this does not make the whole motion linear. These are properties of the model and its derivatives; they do not establish biological intent, individual muscle recruitment, or optimal swing technique.
